body: the alcohol wipes and briefcase are wrapped in a child's raincoat. one stayed dry while the other was left in road mud.
title: missing count beside the alcohol wipes

body: Farm diary: the first fire started beneath the assay table after a field sample cracked. The wet soil burned blue before any building caught.
title: First fire under the assay table

body: Diary entry: beside the second fire mark lay a scorched tray from the soil assay. Its unburned label says the orchard batch was reapplied after rain.
title: Second fire, scorched assay tray

body: Photograph back: the third fire began among returned seed sacks, not the nearby lumber. Violet grains remained in the seams after the flames went out.
title: Third fire, seed sacks first

body: Farm log: smoke at the fourth fire rose from the rinse pit after the trial crew emptied its hoses. The grass died in a clean ring before dusk.
title: Fourth fire beside the rinse pit

body: Torn notebook page: the fifth fire followed a split treatment drum. Water spread the burning film, so we covered it with field soil and left.
title: Fifth fire after the drum split

body: Receipt margin: replace two boots burned at the sixth fire on the sampling route. Both soles carried the same sticky amber residue.
title: Sixth fire on the sample route

body: Letter draft: the seventh fire caught damp hay where the pasture spray settled. The extension worker asked us to call it a lantern accident.
title: Seventh fire at the hay edge

body: Diary line: the eighth fire glowed before sunrise around bags from the night application. No homes were burning and no siren had sounded.
title: Eighth fire before sunrise

body: Photograph note: the ninth fire follows the drainage cut from the experimental plot. Frogs floated below it while the bank still smoked.
title: Ninth fire by the drainage cut

body: Maintenance page: the tenth fire blackened the parked sprayer from beneath. The fuel line was intact; dried treatment foam covered the hot shield.
title: Tenth fire under the sprayer

body: Personal note: after the eleventh fire, every test cage stood open. The rabbits were gone, but their water pans held white crystals.
title: Eleventh fire and empty cages

body: Farm diary: the twelfth fire consumed only the flagged crop rows. Untreated rows on either side stayed green until the next rain.
title: Twelfth fire at the row flags

body: Feed receipt back: at the thirteenth fire we found six empty additive tins behind the shed. The purchase line lists five.
title: Thirteenth fire behind the shed

body: Notebook sketch: the fourteenth fire crawled across wet ground in the same path as yesterday’s trial runoff. Ordinary straw would not burn there.
title: Fourteenth fire along wet ground

body: Letter fragment: beneath the fifteenth fire mark I buried a sealed leaf jar. Its leaves spotted black before the heat reached them.
title: Fifteenth fire and the buried jar

body: Diary line at the sad face: the field cook wept when three workers could not swallow lunch. All had handled the new grain coating that morning.
title: Sad face after the field meal

body: Photograph back at the first gun: a guard watched the sample case while the sick applicator waited outside. The case left before the ambulance came.
title: Gun beside the locked sample case

body: Pay-envelope note at the first happy face: bonus for completing the late spray despite complaints. My hands were numb when I signed.
title: Happy face on the bonus sheet

body: Torn diary page: at the first dead face, stained gloves remained beside a crop-trial badge. The public list later called the wearer an unknown traveler.
title: First dead face, stained gloves

body: Notebook line: the second dead face marks the well tender who sampled cloudy water for the pasture study. His bottle disappeared before dawn.
title: Second dead face by the well

body: Photograph note: the third dead face lies beside corn that looks untouched. A trial flag was pulled from the row but its wire hole remains.
title: Third dead face near clean corn

body: Mileage slip back: the fourth dead face was found on the field truck path. Tire tracks lead away before the road closure begins.
title: Fourth dead face on the truck path

body: Diary entry: the fifth dead face is beside the crew wash basin. The water smelled of bleach and the rinse ledger had been torn out.
title: Fifth dead face and the wash basin

body: Torn letter: at the sixth dead face, orchard netting covered a man still wearing sample tags. The fruit above him had split without ripening.
title: Sixth dead face under orchard netting

body: Receipt note: the seventh dead face fell beside feed mixed for the supplement trial. The cart number is absent from the barn account.
title: Seventh dead face at the feed cart

body: Personal map note: the eighth dead face lay beyond the last trial flag, where the wind carried the mist. Officials later measured only inside the flags.
title: Eighth dead face beyond the flags

body: Notebook page: a sealed flask beside the ninth dead face contains green field water. The label asks for testing, but no laboratory is named.
title: Ninth dead face and the sealed flask

body: Photograph back at the second happy face: the supervisor held up a clean inspection sheet while smoke rose behind the trial rows.
title: Second happy face on a clean report

body: Diary margin at the second gun: an armed man collected the rinse records and left the seed invoices. He wore no county badge.
title: Second gun guarding rinse records

body: Letter fragment at the second sad face: twelve calf tags came back from the supplement pasture, but only eleven calves were unloaded.
title: Second sad face beside calf tags

body: Field log at the first skull: this soil core was rejected for a sharp solvent smell. The replacement core came from outside the treated rows.
title: First skull, rejected soil core

body: Receipt back at the second skull: one rain-barrel sample, paid cash. The barrel stood downwind of the experimental orchard.
title: Second skull, rain-barrel sample

body: Diary line at the third skull: birds dropped beneath the plot wire after dawn spraying. The crew buried them before opening the gate.
title: Third skull, birds under the wire

body: Warehouse note at the fourth skull: the returned treatment drum weighed nine pounds less than dispatch. Its seal appeared untouched.
title: Fourth skull, missing drum weight

body: Farm notebook at the fifth skull: pour away milk from the test pasture until told otherwise. The instruction arrived before the cattle looked ill.
title: Fifth skull, milk poured away

body: Photograph back at the sixth skull: bean leaves blackened in the shape of yesterday’s spray fan. The roots remained pale and firm.
title: Sixth skull, blackened bean leaves

body: Torn ledger at the seventh skull: the final field count omits two applicators and one sample case. Their truck is still marked returned.
title: Seventh skull, final field count
